name: Neck harness lifts

lead: A neck harness holds a weight so the neck can be trained with progressive resistance, the way other muscles are.
Lifters use it to add neck thickness, which they associate with a stronger physique.

paras: Muscle growth from progressive loading of the neck flexors and extensors.
The cervical spine is involved, so form and gradual progression are commonly stressed.

chain: Weighted harness loads the neck muscles
Thicker neck and stronger upper-body look
angle.text: Loading the neck progressively with a harness is intended to add muscle size to the neck and upper traps, which proponents say fills out the neck and frame.

lead: Neck harness lifts are a form of neck training in which a head harness holds a weight plate or chain, and the lifter performs flexion, extension or side-bending against that load. People use them to build the muscles of the neck, which thickens the neck and changes how the head and shoulders look in a physique, and which is popular among combat-sport athletes.

In looksmaxxing and lifting communities, neck size is discussed as part of a stronger, more masculine frame. The practice appears in training logs on forums such as T Nation, where lifters mention neck work alongside presses and pulls.[1][2]

paras: The lifter wears a harness on the head with a weight hanging from it and moves the neck through controlled ranges, commonly extension, flexion and lateral movements. Training logs on lifting forums show neck work being mixed into programmes alongside heavy compound lifts.[1][3]

Community discussion links a thicker neck with a more imposing appearance, and treats the harness as the standard tool for progressive loading. Forum lifters also mention related upper-back work such as pulldowns for posture and shoulder position.[4]
The neck contains the cervical spine, so coaches and clinicians commonly advise gradual progression and attention to technique. Specific injury data are not summarised here.

lore.intro: Neck training appears in lifting logs and physique discussions as an accessory habit.

claims.claim: A bigger neck makes the frame look stronger
